success_patterns: Compare close alternatives as exact logical claims: preserve connective and quantifier scope (for example, both conditions for every radius versus at least one condition at each radius), and distinguish a one-way implication from an equivalence.

Use definitions and admissible boundary cases to distinguish formulas and conclusions that differ by a single detail, such as an included endpoint, denominator, rate, regularity condition, or finite-time versus global claim.

patch.reasoning: The skill already captures exact option comparison and boundary checks. One useful precision is to state the different tail meanings of limsup and liminf explicitly, since confusing them can change whether a blow-up condition is necessary and sufficient.

edits.target: Preserve the exact form of asymptotic assertions: note cutoffs, the order of iterated limits, and whether the claim uses a limit or limsup. Do not silently replace a truncated approximation with convergence to a full series.
edits.content: - Interpret limit operators literally: \(\limsup_{t\to T^-} h(t)=-\infty\) means \(h(t)\to-\infty\), while \(\liminf_{t\to T^-} h(t)=-\infty\) only guarantees arbitrarily late values arbitrarily negative. Do not interchange them unless the hypotheses establish the needed convergence or monotonicity.
